examples.text: GWENDOLEN. […] and my ideal has always been to love someone of the name of Ernest. There is something in that name that inspires absolute confidence.
examples.ref: 1895, Oscar Wilde, The Importance of Being Earnest […] , [Act I]:

examples.text: "What's his name, your boyfriend?" "Ernest. Ernest Hemingway." The name was received in disparaging silence. Marlene said: "You wouldn't get me going out with a feller called Ernest. My granddad was Ernest."

categories: English male given names from Germanic languages
glosses: A male given name from the Germanic languages; popular in the 19th century.
